sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the 
equipment inspection I1, which must be performed every six months as indicated by 
M6 in the title block.

The first draft initiated by eng.Haytham Hemdan, 
tested by eng. Mohamed Abbass & eng. Tamer Awad Abdul Rahman, revised by 
EDEPC quality control 
eng. Adel Abdul Kader El Naggar, approved by eng. Tarek Youssef Ali, Head Sector of 
Ayoun Moussa Power Station.

This 
document accepted by eng. Samir Abd El Gilil EDEPC inspection & quality control 
general director, MPIS coordinator, and 
certified by accountant Mahmoud Soliman EDEPC admin & financial inspection & 
quality control's general director and supervisor of inspection & quality 
control head sector.
Safety Precautions

A work permit must be issued, qualified maintenance 
 staff carry the suitable safety ID category,

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the 
 work area is required,

Ensure engine starting circuits are disabled before commencing service or 
maintenance procedure.
Isolate any anti-condensation heater supply.

sections.text:
NOTE Incorrect speed setting will give 
proportional error in voltage output.
Checking PMG
Start the set and run at rated speed

Measure the voltage at AVR terminals P2, P3 and 
P4. These should be balanced and within the following ranges: 
50HZ generators- 170-180 
volts. 60HZ generators- 200-216 volts.

Should the voltage be unbalanced stop the set, 
remove the MPG sheet metal cover from the non drive end bracket and disconnect 
the multipin plug in the PMG output leads.
Check leads P2, P3, and P4 for continuity.

Check the PMG stator resistances between output 
leads. These should be balanced and within +/-10% of 2.3 ohm. If resistances are 
unbalanced and /or incorrect the PMG stator must be replaced.

If the voltages are balanced but low and PMG 
stator winding resistances are correct the PMG rotor must be replaced.

sections.text:
Checking Generator Windings 
and Rotating Diodes

This procedure is carried out with leads X and XX 
disconnected at AVR or transformer control Rectifier Bridge and using 12 volt d.c supply to leads X and XX.
Start the Set and Run at Rated Speed.

Measure the voltage at the main output terminals 
U, V and W.

If voltages are balanced and within +/-10 % of the 
generator nominal voltage, check voltage at AVR terminals 6, 
7 and 8 these should be balanced and between 170-250 volts.

If voltages at main terminals are balanced but 
voltages at 6, 7 and 8 are unbalanced, check continuity of leads 6, 7 and 8. 
Where an isolating transformer is fitted (MX321 AVR) Check transformer winding.
If faulty the transformer unit must be replaced.

If all voltages are balanced within 1 % 
at main terminals, it can be assumed that all exciter windings, main windings 
and main rotating diodes are in good order, and the fault is in the AVR or 
transformer control.

If voltages are balanced but low, there is a fault in the main 
excitation windings or rotating diodes assembly, proceed as follows to identify.

sections.text: Rectifier Diodes

Check 
the diodes in rectifier assembly with a multimeter, disconnect the flexible 
leads at the terminal end for each diode

Check the forward and reverse resistance, a healthy diode will 
indicate a very high resistance (infinity) in the reverse direction, and low 
resistance in the forward direction, a healthy diode will give a full deflection 
reading in both directions with the test meter on the 10.000 ohms scale, or an 
infinity readings in both directions.

On an electronic digital meter a healthy diode 
will give a low reading in one direction, and high reading in the other.

rows:
The rectifier assembly is 
split into two plates, the positive and 
negative, and the main rotor is connected across this plates.

Each plates 
carries three diodes, the negative plate carrying negative biased diodes and the 
 positive plates carrying positive biased diodes.

sections.text:
Ensure that the
correct polarity diodes are fitted to each respective plate,

When fitting the diodes to the plates they must be tight enough 
to ensure a good mechanical and electrical contact, but should be over 
tightened, the recommended torque tightening is 4.06 - 4.74 NM (36 -42Ib in).

sections.text: Surge Suppressor

The surge suppressor is a metal-oxide varistor connected across 
the two rectifier plates to prevent high transient reverse voltages in the field 
windings from damaging the diodes

This device is not polarized and will show a virtually infinite reading in both 
directions with an ordinary resistance meter. If defective this will be visible 
by inspection, since it will normally fail to short circuit and show signs of 
disintegration, Replace it fully

Voltages

leads U1 U2, (U5 U6), V1 V2, (V5 V6), W1 W2, (W5 W6) to isolate each winding 
section.

Leads suffixed 5 and 6 apply to 
12 wire winding only

sections.text:
Excitation 
Control Test
AVR Function Test

All types of AVRs can be tested 
within this procedure:

Remove exciter field leads X and XX (F1 & F2) from the 
AVR terminals X & XX (F1 & F2)

Connect a 60w 24v household lamp to AVR terminals X& XX 
(F1 & F2)
Set the AVR volts control potentiometer fully clockwise

Connect a 12 volts, 1.0A DC supply to the exciter field 
leads X & XX (F1& F2) with X (F1) to the positive
Start the generating set and run at rated speed

Check that the generator output voltage is within +/- 10% 
of rated voltage

sections.text: Notes:

If the generator output voltage is correct but the 
voltage on 7-8 (or P2 P3) is low, check auxiliary leads and connection to main 
terminals

The lamp connected across X-XX should glow. In the 
case of MX321 AVRs the lamp should glow for approximately 8 sec. and then turn 
off. Failure to turn off indicates faulty protection circuit and the AVR should 
be replaced

Turning the volts control potentiometer fully 
anti-clockwise should turn off the lamp with all AVR types

Should the lamp fail to light the AVR is faulty 
and should be replaced

AVR terminals X & XX (F1 & F2)

(F1 & F2)
Set the AVR volts control potentiometer fully clockwise
Connect a 12 volts, 1.0A DC supply to the exciter field 
leads X & XX (F1& F2) with X (F1) to the positive
Start the generating set and run at rated speed
Check that the generator output voltage is within +/- 10% 
of rated voltage

off. Failure to turn off indicates faulty protection circuit and the AVR should 
be replaced
Turning the volts control potentiometer fully 
anti-clockwise should turn off the lamp with all AVR types
